title: Include the primary content in the initial HTML response
statement: The main content of each indexable route is present in the response body as delivered, before any client script runs, rather than fetched and inserted afterwards.
rationale: Any consumer that reads the response without executing script sees whatever the body contains at that moment, so a body holding only a mount point describes a page with no content regardless of what the browser later shows.
implementation: Move the route from a purely client-rendered mode into the framework's server-rendered or prerendered mode, fetching the data during the render rather than in an effect after mount. Where a route genuinely cannot render on the server, record that and do not present it as indexable.

verification.method: Fetch each route with script execution disabled and compare the visible text of the delivered body against the text present after hydration.

title: Keep primary content readable before hydration completes
statement: The delivered markup is styled and laid out well enough to read on its own, so the interval before the client bundle attaches shows the content rather than a blank region, a spinner, or a skeleton standing in for text the response already carried.
rationale: Content delivered but hidden until script attaches is content nobody can use during the wait, and on a slow device or a failed bundle load that wait never ends.
implementation: Ship the styles the delivered markup needs without waiting for the bundle, and do not gate visibility of server-rendered content on a mounted flag. Reserve loading placeholders for regions whose data really is fetched after load.

verification.method: Load each route with the client bundle request blocked and record what content remains visible and usable.

caution: The cited article describes rendering trade-offs rather than stating a requirement, so this record is tier B. It is included because the failure it prevents is observable in the browser, not because a platform mandates it.

title: Do not mutate canonical or robots directives from client script
statement: The canonical link and any index-controlling directive are written by the server render and are not added, removed, or rewritten by client code after the document loads.
rationale: A directive that only exists after script execution may never be observed, and one that changes after load leaves two different answers to the same question, with no way for the site to know which was read.
implementation: Compute both values during the server render for every route, including routes reached through client navigation, and delete any client-side head manipulation that touches them. A client router changing the address must trigger a render that produces the correct values, not a patch applied to the previous document.

verification.method: Compare the canonical link and index directives in the unexecuted response body against those present after load and after a client-side navigation.

title: Map client-side route failures onto accurate status codes
statement: A route the application resolves as missing or failed returns the corresponding status code from the server, rather than returning success and rendering an error state in the body.
rationale: A successful status with an error body is indistinguishable from a real page to anything reading the status line, so missing routes accumulate in the index as pages that exist and say nothing.
implementation: Resolve existence during the server render and return the correct status from that path, using the framework's not-found signal rather than rendering a not-found component under a success status. For a static export where the host controls the status, configure the host to serve the error document with the right code.

verification.method: Request known missing and failing routes and record the status code returned alongside the content rendered.

title: Back infinite scroll with crawlable paginated URLs
statement: A list that loads more items as the reader scrolls also exposes each batch at its own URL reachable through an anchor, and requesting that URL directly returns the same items the scroll would have appended.
rationale: Items appended by a scroll handler exist only inside the session that scrolled, so a list that grows only on scroll has exactly one crawlable page no matter how many items it contains.
implementation: Give each batch a URL the server can render on its own and link to the next batch with an anchor, then let the scroll handler enhance that link rather than replace it. Keep the item ordering stable so a given URL returns the same batch on a later request.

verification.method: Request each batch URL directly and compare the items returned against those the scroll interaction appends at the same position.
